requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields, not directly referred to in the notation shall remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a variable that is not assigned explicitly IS uninitialized.
requirements.original: When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: The optional attribute SHALL NOT have any effect on variables.
requirements.original: When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", optional fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL implicitly be set to `omit`.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", mandatory fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In value list notation for a record value, every field listed SHALL be specified with a value, the not used symbol "-" or the `omit` keyword.
requirements.original: When using the value list notation, all fields listed in the notation shall be specified either with a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: In value list notation, the `omit` keyword SHALL only be used for optional fields.
requirements.original: The omit keyword shall only be used for optional fields.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: An optional field given `omit` in value list notation IS not present in the resulting value.
requirements.original: Its result is that the given field is not present in the given value.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In value list notation, the n-th list component (a value, "-" or `omit`) IS associated with the n-th field of the record type.
requirements.original: The first component of the list (a value, a "-" or omit) is associated with the first field, the second list component is associated with the second field, etc.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: A value list notation SHALL NOT contain an empty assignment (two commas immediately following each other or separated only by white space).
requirements.original: No empty assignment is allowed (i.e. two commas, the second immediately following the first or only with white space between them).

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: In value list notation, a field to be left unchanged that is followed by fields assigned a value or template explicitly SHALL be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: Fields to be left unchanged, but followed by fields to which a value or template is assigned explicitly, shall be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: When value list notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", the remaining fields at the end of the type definition missing from the notation ARE left unchanged.
requirements.original: When using value list notation in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", all remaining fields at the end of the type definition, missing from the value list notation, are left unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: When value list notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", an optional field to be omitted by the implicit mechanism that is followed by explicitly assigned fields SHALL be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: When using value list notation in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", optional fields wished to be omitted by the implicit mechanism, but followed by fields to which a value or template is assigned explicitly, shall be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit" and all trailing fields are optional
requirements.canonical: When all remaining fields at the end of the type definition are optional and are to be omitted by the implicit omit mechanism, the not used symbol "-" MAY be used for some or all of them, or they MAY be left out of the value list notation.
requirements.original: When all remaining fields at the end of the type definition are optional and they are wished to be omitted by the implicit mechanism, either the not used symbol "-" can be used for some or all of them or they can simply be left out from the notation.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value is assigned from a referenced value in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the uninitialized optional fields of the referenced value SHALL be set to `omit` in the new value.
requirements.original: When using direct assignment notation in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the uninitialized optional fields in the referenced value, shall implicitly be set to omit after the assignment in the new value, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'direct assignment notation' is not a defined term; it means assigning a reference to an existing value (e.g. c_x4 := c_x3).

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value is assigned from a referenced value in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the mandatory fields SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When using direct assignment notation in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the uninitialized optional fields in the referenced value, shall implicitly be set to omit after the assignment in the new value, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'direct assignment notation' is not a defined term; it means assigning a reference to an existing value.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-modifier
requirements.canonical: A field assignment in a record value or template MAY be prefixed by the `@fuzzy` modifier.
requirements.original: A field assignment in a record value or template can be prefixed by the @fuzzy modifier to declare that the right hand side of the assignment shall only be evaluated when used in a matching, receiving or sending operation, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy operand to an expression, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy actual parameter or on the right-hand-side of an assignment to a non-lazy or non-fuzzy variable, template variable or template.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-modifier
requirements.canonical: The right hand side of a `@fuzzy` field assignment SHALL only be evaluated when used in a matching, receiving or sending operation, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy operand of an expression, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy actual parameter, or on the right hand side of an assignment to a non-lazy or non-fuzzy variable, template variable or template.
requirements.original: A field assignment in a record value or template can be prefixed by the @fuzzy modifier to declare that the right hand side of the assignment shall only be evaluated when used in a matching, receiving or sending operation, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy operand to an expression, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy actual parameter or on the right-hand-side of an assignment to a non-lazy or non-fuzzy variable, template variable or template.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: A field of a record SHALL be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.ElementId.
requirements.original: Elements of a record shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.ElementId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a structured type or an expression of a structured type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

ambiguity.issue: 'elements' is used where record 'fields' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: In a dot notation, TypeIdOrExpression SHALL resolve to the name of a structured type or to an expression of a structured type, such as a variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template or function invocation.
requirements.original: Elements of a record shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.ElementId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a structured type or an expression of a structured type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: In a dot notation, ElementId SHALL resolve to the name of a field of the structured type.
requirements.original: ElementId shall resolve to the name of a field in the structured type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: A field of a record type definition SHALL NOT reference itself in its type (e.g. `MyType.field2 field2`).
requirements.original: Fields of record type definitions shall not reference themselves.

ambiguity.issue: 'reference themselves' may mean only a field type that references the same field via dot notation (as in the example) or any (also indirect) circular field-type reference; recursive record types via optional fields are allowed elsewhere. The direct reading matching the example was chosen.
readings: A field type of a record type definition SHALL NOT be a reference to that same field (e.g. `MyType.field2 field2`).
A field type of a record type definition SHALL NOT directly or indirectly depend on the field itself.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: The type of a field of a record type or record subtype referenced by dot notation IS the set of values allowed by the constraints of the field declaration itself.
requirements.original: If a field in a record type or a subtype of a record type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that field imposed by the constraints of the field declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the **record type itself are ignored).**

requirements.subject: ent:subtype-constraint
requirements.canonical: Subtype constraints applied to the record type itself ARE ignored when a field type is referenced by dot notation.
requirements.original: If a field in a record type or a subtype of a record type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that field imposed by the constraints of the field declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the **record type itself are ignored).**

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: Referencing a subfield of an uninitialized or omitted record field or value on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Referencing a subfield of an uninitialized or omitted record field or value on the right hand side of an assignment shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: When a field of an uninitialized record value or field, or of an omitted field (also omitted at a higher level), is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: When referencing a field of an uninitialized record value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded, the subfield referenced in the dot notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record type, the subfield referenced in the dot notation shall be set to present and all unreferenced mandatory subfields shall be left uninitialized; when the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be left undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded, all unreferenced mandatory subfields SHALL be left uninitialized.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record type, the subfield referenced in the dot notation shall be set to present and all unreferenced mandatory subfields shall be left uninitialized; when the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be left undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded in a scope where the optional attribute is "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields SHALL be left uninitialized.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record type, the subfield referenced in the dot notation shall be set to present and all unreferenced mandatory subfields shall be left uninitialized; when the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be left undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded in a scope where the optional attribute is "implicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields SHALL be set to `omit`.
requirements.original: When the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "implicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be set to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: Expansion of record of, set of and array values SHALL follow clause 6.2.7, expansion of union values SHALL follow clause 6.2.5.1, and expansion of set values SHALL follow clause 6.2.2.1.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record of/set of/array, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

ambiguity.issue: 'item a) in clauses ... correspondingly' is unclear: clause 6.2.2.1 has no item a) and refers back to 6.2.1.1; it is unclear whether one rule applies to all three type groups or each group maps to one clause. The pairwise mapping was chosen.
readings: Expansion of record of/set of/array values SHALL follow 6.2.7, union values 6.2.5.1, and set values 6.2.2.1 (pairwise).
Expansion of all these values SHALL follow item a) of each of the clauses 6.2.7, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced subfield.

non_requirement.reason: pointer to clause 15.5 for @fuzzy field modifier rules
